title: Emergence of a Tripartite Thermodynamic Landscape in Finite Fermion Systems Beyond the Thermodynamic Limit
content: We investigate the microscopic mechanisms driving temperature-induced macroscopic order within a closed, finite SU(2) spin-flip fermionic system through the framework of quantum information geometry. Remarkably, despite the highly restricted and finite nature of this small-scale architecture, the system is shown to partition cleanly into three distinct thermodynamic regimes: an uncorrelated high-temperature gas phase, an intermediate entropic-slaving domain driven by state-space rank collapse, and a highly ordered coherent condensate at low temperatures. This tripartite landscape demonstrates that macroscopic structural transitions can be rigorously defined and tracked even beyond the conventional thermodynamic limit (N → ∞). While traditional statistical mechanics treats structural coupling constants as rigid external parameters, we demonstrate that within the intermediate thermal window (3.89 < β < 26.83 for N = 4), the system collapses from a two-dimensional control plane into a set of localized, one-dimensional implicit trajectories where parameter autonomy is entirely lost. By resolving the metric singularity (det g = 0), we prove that the nominal statistical manifold reduces to a strict two-state Bernoulli system governed exclusively by two fully Cooper-paired superconducting configurations. Under this constraint, we derive the exact hyperbolic trajectory of the effective coupling constant Veff(β) and analytically extract the universal level-crossing asymptote, Vc = -1.000, representing the sharp quantum boundary where the internal energy gap vanishes. Crucially, we connect the system's informational entropy (S) directly to this hyperbolic trajectory, demonstrating that the system's internal drive to maximize entropy forces the interaction handle to become a statistical slave to the thermal bath. Finally, we analyze the physical reconfigurations and the breaking of score field symmetry that occur when drifting away from this maximum entropy line V ≠−1). Our results firmly establish that what manifests as a mathematical rank-collapse in parameter space corresponds physically to a robust pairing phase transition, showing that informational entropy can natively function as an active organizer of macroscopic quantum coherence. Ultimately, entropic slaving acts as the missing physical bridge connecting the microscopic quantum fluctuations of the system with its emerging macroscopic order.
